en.title: IATA 2026 survey: biometrics go mainstream and AI joins trip planning, but entry rules deter more travelers
en.summary: IATA's 2026 Global Passenger Survey, based on more than 10,000 responses from over 200 countries, found 58% of passengers experienced biometrics in the past year and 49% used AI for travel planning, while 43% said immigration requirements had discouraged them from visiting a destination, up from 33% in 2025.
body: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) released the results of its 2026 Global Passenger Survey (GPS), based on more than 10,000 responses from more than 200 countries. Nearly six in ten passengers reported experiencing biometrics at least once in the past 12 months: 58% had done so, up from 50% in 2025 and 24 percentage points higher than in 2022, and 87% of those who experienced biometrics said they were happy with the experience. Interest in digital passports is also strong, with 84% interested in using a digital passport for online check-in instead of a physical passport, and 78% willing to share biometric information if it means skipping showing a passport or boarding pass at airport checkpoints.

Almost half of travelers, 49%, have used AI for travel planning, most commonly to search for flights to a specific destination (21%), find the cheapest flights (19%), or get inspiration for where to travel (17%). At the same time, entry requirements are a growing barrier: 43% of passengers said immigration requirements had discouraged them from visiting a destination, up from 33% in 2025, and among those deterred, 53% said the process was too complex. Asia-Pacific travelers reported the highest overall satisfaction at 90%, and were the second most willing of any region to use biometrics, while European travelers reported the lowest overall satisfaction at 84%.

facts.claim: The 2026 Global Passenger Survey is based on more than 10,000 responses from more than 200 countries.
58% of passengers experienced biometrics at some point in their airport journey in the past 12 months, up from 50% in 2025, and 87% of those who experienced biometrics were happy with the experience.

84% of travelers are interested in using a digital passport for online check-in instead of their physical passport, and 78% would share biometric information if it means skipping showing a passport or boarding pass at airport checkpoints.
49% of travelers have used AI for travel planning, including 21% to search for flights to a specific destination, 19% to find the cheapest flights, and 17% to get inspiration for where to travel.
Immigration requirements have discouraged 43% of passengers from visiting a destination, up from 33% in 2025, and 53% of those deterred said the process was too complex.
Asia-Pacific travelers reported the highest overall satisfaction at 90%, while European travelers reported the lowest at 84%.

zh.title: IATA2026年全球旅客調查：生物辨識走向普及、AI走入行程規劃，入境規定卻讓更多旅客卻步
zh.summary: IATA2026年全球旅客調查訪問逾10,000名來自200多個國家與地區的旅客，發現過去一年曾使用生物辨識的旅客占58％、曾以AI規劃旅程者占49％，但曾因入境規定而放棄前往某目的地者占43％，高於2025年的33％。
body: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）公布2026年全球旅客調查（GPS）結果，調查訪問逾10,000名來自200多個國家與地區的旅客。過去12個月內曾在機場旅程中至少使用一次生物辨識的旅客占58％，高於2025年的50％，也比2022年高出24個百分點；曾使用生物辨識的旅客中，87％表示對體驗感到滿意。旅客對數位護照的興趣同樣強勁，84％有興趣以數位護照取代實體護照辦理線上報到，78％願意分享生物辨識資訊，以換取在機場檢查點免出示護照或登機證。
近半數旅客曾以AI規劃旅程，占比49％，最常見用途為搜尋前往特定目的地的航班（21％）、尋找最便宜航班（19％）與尋找旅遊靈感（17％）。與此同時，入境規定正成為愈來愈大的出行障礙：43％的旅客表示曾因入境規定而放棄前往某目的地，高於2025年的33％，其中53％認為流程過於複雜。分區來看，亞太旅客整體滿意度最高，達90％，且使用生物辨識的意願居各區第二；歐洲旅客整體滿意度最低，為84％。
